PCR vs Certification: Navigating Amazon's New Non‑GMO Requirements for Dietary Supplements  October 23, 2026 Amazon now requires all non-GMO claims for dietary supplements to be substantiated. Acceptable supporting evidence may include a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test or certification issued under an Amazon-recognized third-party program such as IGEN™. Without valid substantiation, brands risk having 'non-GMO' claims removed, product listings suppressed or products removed from sale. For brands selling dietary supplements on Amazon, it is therefore important to identify an efficient way to meet these requirements while minimizing delays and administrative burdens. PCR or certification? While Amazon accepts both seller-supplied PCR testing and third-party certification as valid evidence of non-GMO claim substantiation, these two options offer very different operational and commercial outcomes for brands. PCR testing provides point-in-time verification and places ongoing responsibility on the brand, including managing documents, maintaining records and ensuring substantiation remains current as products, suppliers and formulations evolve. As a result, PCR testing typically serves as standalone evidence of non-GMO status, without delivering additional program or marketing benefits. Certification programs, by contrast, provide a more comprehensive, structured framework that supports substantiation requirements while offering ongoing oversight, consumer-facing recognition, and broader marketing value beyond Amazon compliance. Depending on the program, certification may also streamline enrollment and create recognizable trust signals that strengthen consumer confidence and brand positioning.
